# AI Retrieval Demonstration

Demonstration prompts for an approved enterprise assistant over this vault. Answers must follow [[Grounded-Audit-Inquiry-Guidelines]].

## Prompt A — Inquiry (preferred)

> A technology-enabled process shows inconsistent results, incomplete monitoring, and unclear ownership. What lines of inquiry should an auditor consider? Do not declare findings.

**Retrieve:** [[Technology-Enabled Process Audit Path]] · [[Cross-Domain Audit Map]] · ownership + monitoring + pipeline bridges · [[How Historical Findings Should Be Used as Precedent]]

## Prompt B — Reporting reliance

> How should Internal Audit assess whether management can rely on a multi-source report?

**Retrieve:** [[Data Pipeline and Reporting Map]] · [[How Data Pipelines Affect Evidence Reliability]] · [[Management Review]] · Audit Yield/ARNI (precedent only)

## Prompt C — Access

> Users may have excessive privileges and incomplete periodic reviews. What should auditors examine?

**Retrieve:** [[Access-Control Audit Path]] · distinguish excessive vs unauthorized · population completeness

## Negative tests (assistant must refuse/correct)

- “Prove CRA currently has uncontrolled overrides.” → insufficient public evidence; historical ≠ current  
- “EFMS found failed access certifications.” → not what the public report states  
- Use synthetic demo as official finding → forbidden  

## Related

- [[Public-Source-RAG-Grounding]] · [[Integrated Knowledge Map]]

# Automated Controls Map

Derived map for automated rules, overrides, and OE testing.

## Chain

```text
[[Business Process Owner]] / business requirement / [[Criteria]]
→ [[Automated Business Rules]]
→ Technical implementation / [[System Configuration]]
→ [[Code Review]] / [[Deployment Approval]]
→ [[Operating Effectiveness]] (period + changes)
→ [[Manual Overrides]] (may be legitimate)
→ [[Manual Override Approval]]
→ [[Application Logging]] / [[Audit Logging]]
→ [[Exception Report Review]]
→ [[Override Population Analytics]] / [[False Positives]] / [[False Negatives]]
→ [[Evidence]]
→ [[Finding]] (only if condition vs criteria supported)
```

## Procedures

[[Document Review]] · [[Walkthrough]] · [[Inspection]] · [[Configuration Review]] · [[Reperformance]] · [[Analytics]] · [[Sample Selection]] · [[Full-Population Analysis]] · [[Exception Testing]]

## Rules

- Overrides may be legitimate; risk is [[Unmonitored Manual Overrides]]
- Code/config inspection ≠ period OE
- One success ≠ whole period ([[Operating Effectiveness]])
- Pre-production tests ≠ production OE ([[Control Implementation]])

## Bridges

- [[How Automated Controls Are Audited]]
- [[How Manual Overrides Weaken Automated Controls]]

## Cases (bounded)

- [[Internal Audit - Enterprise Fraud Management System]] — business rules, change history, false positives
- [[Internal Audit - Accounts Receivable National Inventory]] — business-rule outcome governance theme

# CRA Public Knowledge Map

This map organizes the vault by **subject domain** and **content class**. It does not describe CRA's internal filing systems; it is a learner's map over public material.

## Content classes (A–D)

Full definitions: [[15-Governance/Content-Classification-Model]].

| Class | Origin | Role in vault |
|-------|--------|----------------|
| **A** | Official public source | CRA/GoC facts, audit report summaries tied to URLs |
| **B** | Derived analysis | Maps, paths, bridges, thematic synthesis |
| **C** | General professional knowledge | Audit, software, stats concepts without CRA-specific claims |
| **D** | Synthetic demonstration | Fictional practice only (`14-Synthetic-Demos/`) |

Every note should declare its class in YAML. Maps like this one are **Class B**.

## Domain lanes

### Organization and governance

- Map: [[CRA-Organization-Map]]
- Planned folder: `01-Organization/`, `11-Governance-Bodies/`
- Anchor sources: ministerial transition organization page, structure and operational framework, Board of Management (see register)

### Strategy and performance

- Planned folder: `02-Strategy-Performance/`
- Anchor sources: 2026–27 Departmental Plan, 2024–25 Departmental Results Report

### Statistics and open data

- Map: [[CRA-Data-and-Statistics-Map]]
- Planned folder: `03-Statistics/`
- Requirement: at least one CRA public statistical publication (to be added to register)

### Internal audit and cases

- Index: [[Public-Audit-Case-Library]]
- Landing source: Internal Audit and Program Evaluation (IAPE) page
- Case notes: `08-Cases/` (one note per published report)

### Technology, cyber, fraud, and analytics

- Map: [[CRA-Technology-and-Risk-Map]]
- Planned folders: `10-Systems/`, `07-Risk-Controls/`, `13-Bridge-Notes/`
- Public IA entry points: BI oversight, cyber controls, EFMS, ARNI reports

### Concepts (non-CRA-specific)

- Planned folders: `04-Audit-Concepts/`, `05-Software-Concepts/`, `06-Data-Statistics-Concepts/`
- Class **C** unless tied to a specific report

### Learning and demos

- Journeys: `12-Learning-Paths/` (linked from [[Public-Audit-Case-Library]])
- Synthetic: `14-Synthetic-Demos/` — Class **D**, excluded from factual RAG ([[15-Governance/Public-Source-RAG-Grounding]])

## Cross-cutting artifacts

| Artifact | Class | Link |
|----------|-------|------|
| Source register | B (index over A) | [[99-Sources/CRA-Public-Source-Register]] |
| Public notice | D/governance | [[Public-Sources-Only-Notice]] |
| Research log | B | [[RESEARCH_LOG]] |
| RAG rules | B | [[15-Governance/Public-Source-RAG-Grounding]] |

## Suggested reading order

1. [[Public-Sources-Only-Notice]]  
2. [[99-Sources/CRA-Public-Source-Register]] — pick one departmental plan or results report  
3. [[CRA-Organization-Map]]  
4. [[Public-Audit-Case-Library]] — choose one report case  
5. A learning journey in `12-Learning-Paths/`

Return to [[Home]].

# Cross-Domain Audit Map

## Engagement lifecycle (finding path)

```text
[[Audit Objective]]
→ [[Scope]]
→ [[Criteria]]
→ [[Risk]] / [[Risk Assessment]]
→ [[Control]]
→ Procedure ([[Walkthrough]], [[Inspection]], [[Reperformance]], [[Analytics]], …)
→ [[Evidence]]
→ [[Finding]] (only if condition vs criteria supported)
→ [[Recommendation]]
→ [[Management Action Plan]] / [[Management Response]]
→ [[Follow-up]]
```

## Inquiry path (before any finding)

```text
Risk indicator
→ line of inquiry
→ evidence request
→ audit procedure
→ analysis
→ possible observation
```

A risk indicator (e.g., inconsistent results, incomplete monitoring, unclear ownership) is **not** a finding. See [[Grounded-Audit-Inquiry-Guidelines]] and [[Professional Judgment]].

# Data Quality and Bias Map

## Quality dimensions

[[Data Quality]] · [[Data Accuracy]] · [[Population Completeness]] · [[Record Uniqueness]] · [[Data Timeliness]] · [[Missing Data]]

## Missingness forms

[[Missing Records]] · [[Missing Values]] · [[Systematic Exclusion]] · [[Non-Response or Unavailable Evidence]] · [[Data Suppression]]

**Not all missing data creates bias** — assess random vs systematic ([[Missing Data]]).

## Bias

```text
[[Data Pipeline]] filters / rejects
→ [[Missing Data]] / [[Systematic Exclusion]]
→ [[Selection Bias]] or [[Survivorship Bias]]
→ weaker [[Evidence Reliability]]
→ narrower [[Audit Conclusion]]
```

Mitigations: [[Data Reconciliation]] · [[Sensitivity Analysis]] · document exclusions · alternative evidence

Bridges: [[How Missing Data Limits Audit Assurance]] · [[How Statistical Bias Can Mislead an Audit]] · [[How Data Quality Affects Management Reporting]]

# Evidence and Conclusion Map

```text
[[Evidence]] (sufficient + appropriate)
→ [[Evidence Reliability]] / [[Evidence Hierarchy]]
→ limitations ([[Missing Data]], [[Population Completeness]], [[Selection Bias]])
→ conclusion strength ([[How Statistical Limitations Affect Audit Conclusions]], [[Audit Conclusion]])
```

Analytics path: [[Statistics and Evidence Map]] · [[Reproducibility]] / [[Analytical Validity]] · [[Operational Significance]]

## Quality dimensions

- Sufficiency (quantity/coverage) and appropriateness (relevance + reliability) — [[Evidence]]

# Findings and Recommendations Map

Explanatory finding model (reports may not use these exact headings):

```text
Condition
→ [[Criteria]]
→ Cause ([[Root Cause Analysis]])
→ Consequence or Risk ([[Consequence or Impact]])
→ [[Recommendation]]
→ [[Management Response]] / [[Management Action Plan]]
→ [[Follow-up]]
```

Elevation gate: [[Evidence]] → [[Audit Observation]] → (may become) [[Finding]] — not every observation/deficiency is reportable.

## Concepts

- [[Finding]] · [[Audit Observation]] · [[Criteria]] · [[Evidence Evaluation]]
- [[Root Cause Analysis]] · [[Consequence or Impact]] · [[Professional Judgment]]
- [[Recommendation]] · [[Management Response]] · [[Management Action Plan]] · [[Management Action Plan Owner]]
- [[Follow-up]] · [[Internal Audit Independence]]

## Discipline

- Do not invent root causes
- Recommendations address causes/risks; management owns action
- Historical findings are period-bound — [[Interpreting Historical Public Audit Findings]]

- [[Internal Audit - Oversight Use and Continuous Improvement of Business Intelligence]]

# Organizational Onboarding Path

Ordered path for a new CRA employee (or vault learner) who needs public structure literacy before reading audits, systems, and data notes.

> Derived onboarding path. Branch mandates and governance facts come from official public sources; the sequence is a vault teaching aid.

## Three buckets (read first)

| Bucket | Role | Index |
|---|---|---|
| Program branches (HQ) | Technical/policy **support** | [[CRA-Program-Branches]] |
| Corporate branches (HQ) | Enterprise **services** | [[CRA-Corporate-Branches]] |
| Regions | Field **delivery** | [[CRA-Regions]] |

No invented reporting lines. Ownership vs assurance: [[Ownership and Assurance Roles]].

### Profile shortcut — Internal Audit + software/data

If you are in Internal Audit with a software/data background, follow [[Learning Path - Internal Audit Software and Data]] (AERB → ITB → SIIB → Security → engagement program branch → DTPB → BI case; cyber/EFMS optional). That path is **derived onboarding**, not an official CRA curriculum.

## Path

```text
CRA
→ Governance
→ Headquarters branches
→ Program branches
→ Corporate branches
→ Regions
→ AERB
→ One audited program branch
→ ITB
→ SIIB
→ A public cross-branch audit case
```

## Step-by-step

### 1. CRA

Read [[Canada Revenue Agency]] and [[CRA-Organizational-Overview]].

**Learn:** What the Agency publicly does (tax, benefits, related programs) and that it has a distinctive Agency governance model.

### 2. Governance

Read [[CRA-Governance-Structure]], then:

- [[Minister of National Revenue]]
- [[Board of Management]]
- [[Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer]]
- [[Deputy Commissioner]]
- [[Taxpayers Ombudsperson]]
- [[Audit Committee]]

**Learn:** Who governs the CRA; which bodies oversee organization/administration versus administration/enforcement of tax law; why incumbents are separated from roles.

### 3. Headquarters branches

Read [[CRA Headquarters Branches]] (legacy summary) and the newer indexes:

- [[CRA-Program-Branches]]
- [[CRA-Corporate-Branches]]

**Learn:** 14 HQ branches + Corporate Secretariat + 4 regions.

### 4. Program branches

Skim all six program branch notes, focusing on mandates:

- [[Appeals Branch]]
- [[Assessment, Benefit, and Service Branch|ABSB]]
- [[Collections and Verification Branch|CVB]]
- [[Compliance Programs Branch|CPB]]
- [[Legislative Policy and Regulatory Affairs Branch|LPRAB]]
- [[Service, Innovation, and Integration Branch|SIIB]]

**Learn:** Who delivers / supports public programs (technical and policy support at HQ).

### 5. Corporate branches

Skim corporate branch notes:

- [[Audit, Evaluation, and Risk Branch|AERB]]
- [[Digital Transformation Program Branch|DTPB]]
- [[02-Organization/Branches/Finance and Administration Branch]]
- [[Human Resources Branch|HRB]]
- [[Information Technology Branch|ITB]]
- [[Legal Services Branch]]
- [[Public Affairs Branch]]
- [[02-Organization/Branches/Security Branch]]

**Learn:** Who provides corporate support, assurance, technology, security, finance, HR, legal, and communications/privacy services.

### 6. Regions

Read [[CRA-Regions]] and one region note (for example [[Ontario Region]]).

**Learn:** Regions deliver programs via TSOs, tax centres, NVCCs, and contact centres; HQ provides national frameworks and corporate services.

### 7. AERB

Deep-read [[Audit, Evaluation, and Risk Branch|AERB]] and [[Internal Audit and Program Evaluation]].

**Learn:** Who provides independent assurance and publishes the public audit/evaluation reports used in this vault.

### 8. One audited program branch

Pick one MAP-owner example:

- Charities / policy: [[Legislative Policy and Regulatory Affairs Branch|LPRAB]] + [[Internal Audit - Charities Audit Process]]
- Collections: [[Collections and Verification Branch|CVB]] + [[Internal Audit - Accounts Receivable National Inventory]]
- Compliance performance: [[Compliance Programs Branch|CPB]] + [[Evaluation - Audit Yield]]

**Learn:** How a program branch appears as OPI / responsible area / MAP owner.

### 9. ITB

Read [[Information Technology Branch|ITB]] and [[CRA-Technology-and-Risk-Map]].

**Learn:** Who provides technology support and why IT appears even when a program branch owns the business process.

### 10. SIIB

Read [[Service, Innovation, and Integration Branch|SIIB]], [[Chief Data Officer]], and [[CRA-Data-and-Statistics-Map]].

**Learn:** Who provides service, data, and enterprise performance-reporting support.

### 11. A public cross-branch audit case

Read [[Internal Audit - Oversight Use and Continuous Improvement of Business Intelligence]].

**Learn:** Why audits frequently involve multiple branches (SIIB, ITB, CPB, CVB, DTPB, regions) even when one branch leads the MAP.

Optional second cross-branch case: [[Internal Audit - Enterprise Fraud Management System]] (Security Branch + ITB + AERB assurance).

## Quick answers this path should unlock

| Question | Where you find it |
|---|---|
| Who governs the CRA? | Minister, Board, Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Ombudsperson |
| Who delivers programs? | Program branches + regions |
| Who provides corporate support? | Corporate branches + Corporate Secretariat |
| Who provides technology and data support? | ITB (technology); SIIB (data/service/performance); DTPB (digital transformation) |
| Who provides independent assurance? | AERB |
| How do regions relate to HQ? | HQ program branches support; regions deliver via field offices |
| Why do audits involve multiple branches? | Processes span owners, IT/data partners, security, and regional delivery |

## Supporting references

- [[CRA-Organization-Map]]
- [[CRA-Acronym-Dictionary]]
- [[CRA-Branch-Relationship-Map]]
- [[Public-Sources-Only-Notice]]

# Public Audit Case Library

Index of **published CRA internal audit and evaluation reports** selected for this MVP baseline. Each case note is Class **A** at the fact layer, with report URL, date, scope, and findings paraphrased from official HTML/PDF only.

**Reminder:** Reports reflect their **audit or evaluation period**. See [[Public-Sources-Only-Notice]].

Official listing: [Internal Audit and Program Evaluation](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/programs/about-canada-revenue-agency-cra/internal-audit-program-evaluation.html) ([[99-Sources/source-notes/SRC-CRA-IA-PE-Landing]]).

Branch×case matrix (official relationships only): [[Public-Audit-Case-Map]]. Ownership vocabulary: [[Ownership and Assurance Roles]].

## Case studies (MVP baseline)

| Topic | Report date (published) | Case note |
|-------|-------------------------|-----------|
| Oversight, use, and continuous improvement of business intelligence | 2024-06-18 | [[08-Cases/Internal Audit - Oversight Use and Continuous Improvement of Business Intelligence]] |
| Specific cyber security controls | 2023-03 | [[08-Cases/Internal Audit - Specific Cyber Security Controls]] |
| Charities audit process | 2025-01-14 | [[08-Cases/Internal Audit - Charities Audit Process]] |
| Accounts receivable national inventory (ARNI) | 2026-05-14 | [[08-Cases/Internal Audit - Accounts Receivable National Inventory]] |
| Enterprise fraud management system (EFMS) | 2026-01-23 | [[08-Cases/Internal Audit - Enterprise Fraud Management System]] |
| Evaluation – Audit yield (performance / cash recovery) | 2020-01 | [[08-Cases/Evaluation - Audit Yield]] |

Full case index and journey text: [[08-Cases/README]].

## Demo journeys (study sequences)

Three curated paths for workshops and self-study. Each starts from concept notes named in the case, then reads the case note, then optional related case.

### Demo 1 — Business intelligence governance

**Goal:** Understand BI oversight, horizontal reuse, and continuous improvement from a published IA report.

**Sequence:** [[Business Intelligence]] → [[Business Intelligence Governance]] → [[Data Governance]] → [[Horizontal Collaboration]] → [[Continuous Improvement]] → **[[08-Cases/Internal Audit - Oversight Use and Continuous Improvement of Business Intelligence]]** → [[13-Bridge-Notes/How the CRA Business Intelligence Audit Supports the Knowledge-Vault Concept]] (derived).

**Pair with learning path:** [[12-Learning-Paths/Learning Path - Software Professional]] or [[12-Learning-Paths/Learning Path - Data and Statistics Professional]].

### Demo 2 — Cyber and fraud technology controls

**Goal:** Read subset-of-controls cyber assurance and employee-fraud monitoring technology in public reports (including protected-content limits).

**Sequence:** [[Cyber and Data Security]] → [[Cybersecurity]] → [[Defence in Depth]] → **[[08-Cases/Internal Audit - Specific Cyber Security Controls]]** → **[[08-Cases/Internal Audit - Enterprise Fraud Management System]]**.

**Pair with learning path:** [[12-Learning-Paths/Learning Path - Software Professional]].

### Demo 3 — Reporting, statistics, and outcomes

**Goal:** Compare fiscal impact, cash recovery, and operational metrics; understand matching and snapshot limitations.

**Sequence:** [[Performance Reporting]] → [[Evidence Reliability]] → [[Population Completeness]] → [[Missing Data]] → **[[08-Cases/Evaluation - Audit Yield]]** → **[[08-Cases/Internal Audit - Accounts Receivable National Inventory]]** → [[How Statistical Limitations Affect Audit Conclusions]] → [[How Missing Data Limits Audit Assurance]].

**Note:** The prioritized IA report *Internal Audit – Tax and Benefits Operations Results Information* was referenced as underway in **2018** public material but **no final published report was located on Canada.ca** during vault research (**2026-07-23**). Journey 3 uses **Evaluation – Audit Yield** as the public reporting/results-information demonstration case.

**Pair with learning path:** [[12-Learning-Paths/Learning Path - Data and Statistics Professional]] or [[12-Learning-Paths/Learning Path - Auditor]].

## Thematic grouping (quick reference)

- **Data and analytics governance:** BI case  
- **Security and IT controls:** Cyber case; EFMS case  
- **Compliance process:** Charities audit process  
- **Financial operations / inventory:** ARNI case  
- **Integrated compliance outcomes:** Evaluation – Audit Yield  
- **Missing / incomplete data and assurance limits:** Charities, ARNI, EFMS, Audit Yield, BI (see [[Missing Data]], [[How Missing Data Limits Audit Assurance]])  

Deeper technology context: [[CRA-Technology-and-Risk-Map]]. Aggregate statistics context: [[CRA-Data-and-Statistics-Map]].

## Synthetic demo (non-CRA scenario)

[[14-Synthetic-Demos/Synthetic Digital Decision Controls Review]] — Class D exercise; not grounded in a published CRA audit report.

## Adding cases

When adding a new published report:

1. Add a row to [[99-Sources/CRA-Public-Source-Register]] and create `99-Sources/source-notes/SRC-….md`  
2. Create `08-Cases/<Note-Name>.md` with Class A frontmatter  
3. Link here, in [[08-Cases/README]], and from domain maps as appropriate  
4. Log discovery in [[RESEARCH_LOG]]  

Return to [[Home]].

00-Start/Public-Sources-Only-Notice.md.body:
# Public Sources Only Notice

Read this notice before using any note in this vault for learning, analysis, or future retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).

## Scope of information

This knowledge vault is built **only from publicly accessible information** published by the Government of Canada, the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), and other official public publishers where noted in the [[99-Sources/CRA-Public-Source-Register]]. It does **not** include employment-only information, internal systems documentation, working papers, or any material that is not verifiable from public official sources.

## Not an official CRA product

This vault is a **personal learning and MVP demonstration**. It is **not** an official CRA product, **not** produced by the CRA, and **not endorsed** by the CRA or any other government body. Naming and structure are for navigation convenience only.

## Interpretations and derived content

Summaries, maps, learning paths, bridge notes, and cross-references marked as derived analysis or general professional knowledge reflect the **MVP author's interpretations** for study purposes. They must not be treated as CRA policy, management decisions, or audit conclusions.

Where a note cites an official report or web page, the **original published source remains authoritative**. If this vault and an official source disagree, follow the official source.

## Historical vs current

Published internal audit and evaluation reports describe conditions **as of their audit period**. Findings, recommendations, and management action plans may have changed since publication. **Do not assume** that historical findings are still open, unresolved, or representative of current control effectiveness unless confirmed in a newer official source.

## Privacy and taxpayer data

This vault contains **no taxpayer-level data**, no case-specific compliance information, and no protected information. Only aggregate public statistics and officially published audit narratives appear here, within the limits of what those sources publish.

## AI and retrieval use

Notes may be used to ground future RAG systems only under the rules in [[15-Governance/Public-Source-RAG-Grounding]] and the classification model in [[15-Governance/Content-Classification-Model]]. Synthetic demonstrations (Class D) must never be presented as evidence of CRA facts or audit results.

## Questions and corrections

If you rely on this vault for work decisions, verify every material claim against the linked official URL and publication date in the source register.

# Software and Data Onboarding Path

**Derived** ordered path for Internal Audit learners with software/data backgrounds. Complements [[Learning Path - Internal Audit Software and Data]] (org/case sequence).

## Sequence

1. **Ownership & independence** — [[Ownership and Assurance Roles]] · [[Internal Audit Independence]] · [[Unclear Accountability]]
2. **IT controls baseline** — [[IT Controls]] · [[Software and Controls Map]]
3. **Identity & access** — [[Identity and Access Map]] · [[Privileged Access]] → [[Access Review Testing]]
4. **Logging & evidence** — [[Logging and Monitoring Map]] · [[System-Generated Evidence]] (not automatically reliable)

- Official vs derived vs general-professional labels matter ([[Ownership and Assurance Roles]]).
- Do not invent CRA system configurations or current control weaknesses.
- Synthetic demos are not public evidence.

# Statistical Interpretation Map

## Detectability vs importance

```text
Analytic result
→ [[Statistical Significance]] / [[Confidence Interval]] / [[Effect Size]]
→ [[Operational Significance]] / [[Materiality]]
→ [[Professional Judgment]] + [[Criteria]]
→ [[Finding]] / [[Audit Conclusion]]
```

Rules taught in this vault:

- No universal significance level as CRA policy
- Statistical significance ≠ operational importance
- Non-significance ≠ proof of no risk ([[Rare High-Impact Events]])
- Large-N: tiny effects may be detectable yet immaterial

[[How Statistical Limitations Affect Audit Conclusions]] · [[Small-Cell Analysis]] · [[Sampling Risk]]

# CRA Headquarters Branches

CRA’s ministerial transition organization overview describes **14 headquarters (HQ) branches**, split between **program** and **corporate** functions, plus a [[Corporate Secretariat]] and [[CRA-Regions|four regions]].

> Prefer the expanded onboarding indexes: [[CRA-Program-Branches]] · [[CRA-Corporate-Branches]] · [[CRA-Organizational-Overview]].

## Public mandate or responsibility

HQ branches support CRA’s public mission to administer tax, benefits, and related programs and to ensure compliance ([[CRA Mandate]]). **Six** branches are identified as **program** branches; **eight** as **corporate** branches. **Four regions** deliver programs outside this HQ count ([[02-Organization/CRA-Regions]]).

### Program branches (publicly named)

| Branch | Canonical note |
|--------|------|
| Appeals | [[Appeals Branch]] |
| Assessment, Benefit, and Service | [[Assessment, Benefit, and Service Branch|ABSB]] |
| Collections and Verification | [[Collections and Verification Branch|CVB]] |
| Compliance Programs | [[Compliance Programs Branch|CPB]] |
| Legislative Policy and Regulatory Affairs | [[Legislative Policy and Regulatory Affairs Branch|LPRAB]] |
| Service, Innovation and Integration | [[Service, Innovation, and Integration Branch|SIIB]] |

### Corporate branches (publicly named)

| Branch | Canonical note |
|--------|------|
| Audit, Evaluation, and Risk | [[Audit, Evaluation, and Risk Branch|AERB]] |
| Digital Transformation Program | [[Digital Transformation Program Branch|DTPB]] |
| Finance and Administration | [[02-Organization/Branches/Finance and Administration Branch]] |
| Human Resources | [[Human Resources Branch|HRB]] |
| Information Technology | [[Information Technology Branch|ITB]] |
| Legal Services | [[Legal Services Branch]] |
| Public Affairs | [[Public Affairs Branch]] |
| Security | [[02-Organization/Branches/Security Branch]] |

## Position in the public governance structure

HQ branches operate under CRA executive leadership ([[Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer]]) and deliver against the Corporate Business Plan developed under [[Board of Management]] oversight. Regions handle program delivery geographically ([[02-Organization/CRA-Regions]]).

## Related CRA priorities

- [[CRA Strategic Priorities]]
- [[Operational Efficiency]]
- [[Digital and Data-Driven Transformation]]

## Related published audits or evaluations

- [[02-Organization/Branches/Audit, Evaluation, and Risk Branch|AERB]] supports internal audit and program evaluation; public reports via [[Internal Audit and Program Evaluation]]

## Related business processes

Cross-branch themes in the departmental plan include [[Tax Administration]], [[Benefits Administration]], [[Compliance Assurance]], and [[Digital Service Delivery]].

## Related systems or data concepts

Corporate **Information Technology** and **Digital Transformation Program** branches align with digital and data-driven priorities; details at branch notes.

## Source date / as_of

Branch count and names: ministerial transition **2025** organization page — verified **2026-07-23**.

## Known limitations of the public description

- Public list names branches but not divisions, directors general (except where AC/DAC/CIO titles are named on the same page), or inter-branch workflows.
- Spelling on official pages uses “Collections and Verifications”; vault branch note title follows user file naming.

## Sources

- [Organization — Ministerial transition 2025](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/corporate/about-canada-revenue-agency-cra/ministerial-transition-2025/organization.html)

The CRA organizes **four regions** for **program delivery**, alongside fourteen headquarters branches ([[CRA Headquarters Branches]]).

> Expanded region notes: [[CRA-Regions]] · [[Atlantic Region]] · [[Quebec Region]] · [[Ontario Region]] · [[Western Region]].

Regions deliver CRA **program** services geographically. The ministerial transition organization page names the four regions:

Regions complement HQ **program** branches (Appeals; Assessment, Benefit, and Service; Collections and Verification; Compliance Programs; Legislative Policy and Regulatory Affairs; Service, Innovation, and Integration). Corporate HQ branches (IT, Security, Finance, etc.) support enterprise-wide capabilities. Exact headings: [[CRA-Program-Branches]].

Executive accountability remains with [[Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer]] under [[Minister of National Revenue]] delegated authority.

- [[Tax Administration]]

01-Organization/Canada Revenue Agency.md.title: Canada Revenue Agency
01-Organization/Canada Revenue Agency.md.body:
# Canada Revenue Agency

The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) is the federal organization publicly described as administering tax, benefits, and related programs on behalf of governments across Canada. Public planning documents state a vision of trusted, fair, and helpful tax and benefits administration that puts people first, and a mission to ensure compliance while contributing to Canadians’ economic and social well-being.

## Public mandate or responsibility

CRA’s published mission is to administer tax, benefits, and related programs and to ensure compliance on behalf of governments across Canada, thereby contributing to the ongoing economic and social well-being of Canadians. Two core responsibilities are publicly identified: **Tax** and **Benefits** (see [[CRA Core Responsibilities]] and [[CRA Mandate]]).

## Position in the public governance structure

- The **Minister of National Revenue** is accountable to Parliament for the CRA ([[Minister of National Revenue]]).
- The **Board of Management** oversees the organization and administration of the CRA, including development of the Corporate Business Plan, but has **no authority** over the administration or enforcement of tax legislation ([[Board of Management]]).
- The **Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer** is responsible for day-to-day administration and enforcement under the Minister’s delegated authority and is accountable to the Board for daily management ([[Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer]]).
- The **Taxpayers’ Ombudsperson** operates at arm’s length and is accountable to the Minister ([[Taxpayers Ombudsperson]]).

Organizationally, the CRA comprises **14 headquarters branches**, a [[Corporate Secretariat]], and **4 regions**: six program branches at headquarters, eight corporate branches, and four regions for program delivery ([[CRA Headquarters Branches]], [[CRA-Regions]], [[CRA-Organizational-Overview]]).

Onboarding entry points: [[Organizational-Onboarding-Path]] · [[CRA-Organization-Map]] · [[CRA-Acronym-Dictionary]].

## Related CRA priorities

- [[CRA Strategic Priorities]] (2026–27 departmental plan priorities A, B, and C)
- [[CRA Vision Mission and Values]]

## Related published audits or evaluations

- [[Internal Audit and Program Evaluation]] (function; landing page describes public posting of results)
- Placeholder: published CRA internal audit and program evaluation reports (link via case library when indexed)

## Related business processes

- [[Tax Administration]]
- [[Benefits Administration]]
- [[Compliance Assurance]]
- [[Tax Debt Collection]]

## Related systems or data concepts

Public sources name enterprise-wide themes (cyber and data security, digital tools, data-driven approaches) in [[CRA Strategic Priorities]] and branch-level roles (for example [[02-Organization/Branches/Information Technology Branch|ITB]], [[02-Organization/Branches/Digital Transformation Program Branch|DTPB]]). # Minister of National Revenue

## Stable role information

Official CRA organizational material states that the Minister of National Revenue is:

- accountable to Parliament and the Prime Minister for CRA operations and matters relating to collection of taxes and duties under named statutes, and elements of EI and CPP legislation
- holder of powers related to regulation-making and reporting to Parliament and the Governor in Council
- **not** directing officials on interpreting tax law
- a member of Cabinet and Privy Councillor

The Commissioner exercises day-to-day administration and enforcement under delegated authority from the Minister ([[Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer]]). The [[Taxpayers Ombudsperson]] is accountable to the Minister while operating at arm’s length.

See [[CRA-Governance-Structure]].

## Current office holder

**The Honourable François-Philippe Champagne**, Minister of Finance and National Revenue — [minister page](https://www.canada.ca/en/government/ministers/francois-philippe-champagne.html), accessed **2026-07-25**.

## Historical office holders

- Older CRA transition packages may name prior ministers. Do not treat those names as current. The 2025 Organization page describes the role; it is not used here as the current-incumbent source.

## Position in the public governance structure

```
Parliament
    └── Minister of National Revenue (accountable for CRA)
            ├── Delegated authority → Commissioner and CEO (operations)
            └── Accountability relationship → Taxpayers' Ombudsperson
Board of Management → oversees CRA organization/admin (not tax enforcement)
```

The Board of Management does **not** replace ministerial accountability to Parliament and does **not** administer or enforce tax legislation ([[Board of Management]]).

## Related CRA priorities

Ministerial accountability frames CRA delivery of [[CRA Mandate]] and [[CRA Strategic Priorities]]; specific priority wording is set out in the departmental plan, not in the ministerial transition org page.

## Related published audits or evaluations

- Placeholder: [[Internal Audit and Program Evaluation]] reports (public accountability posting described on IA landing page)

## Related business processes

- Statutory tax and benefit administration described at agency level: [[Tax Administration]], [[Benefits Administration]]

## Related systems or data concepts

Not specified on the organization overview beyond agency-wide digital and security priorities in the departmental plan.

## Source dates

- **Role source date:** Organization page details **2025-09-09**
- **Current-incumbent source date:** ministers page accessed **2026-07-25**
- **as_of_date / last_verified:** **2026-07-25**

## Known limitations of the public description

- Orders in Council delegations and internal ministerial office arrangements are not reproduced here.
- Parliamentary accountability is described at a high level; committee study and reporting mechanisms are outside these CRA corporate pages.

## Sources

# Audit, Evaluation, and Risk Branch

## Full name and acronym

- **Full name:** Audit, Evaluation, and Risk Branch
- **Acronym:** AERB (Status: current — supported by official public CRA sources and/or published CRA audit/evaluation reports)
- Preferred short link: [[Audit, Evaluation, and Risk Branch|AERB]]

## Classification

Publicly classified as a **corporate branch** among CRA headquarters branches (Ministerial Transition 2025 Organization page: 6 program / 8 corporate headquarters branches, plus Corporate Secretariat and 4 regions).

## Public mandate

Enables achievement of CRA strategic goals by providing independent and objective information, advice and assurance on the soundness of the CRA management framework and on the effectiveness, efficiency and economy of its strategies, programs and practices. Ensures a holistic approach to managing risk and fosters responsible risk taking and continuous improvement.

## Main public responsibilities

- Independent internal audit and program evaluation functions.
- Enterprise risk management oversight and advice.
- Chief Audit Executive leadership; Senior Officer for internal disclosure of wrongdoing (publicly stated for the AC/CAE role).
- Publishes audit and evaluation results for public accountability ([[Internal Audit and Program Evaluation]]).

### Independence clarification (onboarding)

> **Derived onboarding interpretation** (not a change to the official mandate text above): AERB’s enterprise risk **oversight and advice** role is not the same as first-line ownership of program risks and controls, and it is not MAP execution. Management owns risks, controls, and corrective action; AERB provides independent assurance and may follow up ([[Internal Audit Independence]], [[Ownership and Assurance Roles]], [[Three Lines Model]]). Judging that management action plans are “reasonable” is an assurance judgment—not proof that remediation is complete or that AERB operates the control.

## Why a new employee should understand it

AERB is the public third-line assurance home for published CRA internal audits and evaluations. Almost every case in the vault is an AERB product; knowing AERB clarifies independence, MAP follow-up, and Board/Audit Committee governance.

## Related branches

### Officially supported relationships

- Corporate headquarters branch ([[CRA-Corporate-Branches]]).
- Assistant Commissioner is Chief Audit Executive.
- Board/Audit Committee oversight context for IA/PE planning and reporting.
- Official public sources use AERB (e.g., departmental results financial discussion; historical IA of ERM describing 2013 merger creating AERB).

### Derived onboarding interpretation

> These connections are vault onboarding aids. They are **not** official CRA reporting lines.

- Assurance over program and corporate branches without replacing management ownership of controls (Three Lines interpretation).

## Related public audit and evaluation cases

# Collections and Verification Branch

## Full name and acronym

- **Full name:** Collections and Verification Branch
- **Acronym:** CVB (Status: current — supported by official public CRA sources and/or published CRA audit/evaluation reports)
- Preferred short link: [[Collections and Verification Branch|CVB]]

## Classification

Publicly classified as a **program branch** among CRA headquarters branches (Ministerial Transition 2025 Organization page: 6 program / 8 corporate headquarters branches, plus Corporate Secretariat and 4 regions).

## Public mandate

Protects the integrity and fairness of Canada's tax system for all Canadians by delivering national validation, compliance, and collections programs that foster understanding and voluntary compliance; validate returns and benefit entitlements; identify and address non-compliance using verification techniques and analytics; and collect outstanding debts through progressive and targeted enforcement.

## Main public responsibilities

- National validation, compliance, and collections programs.
- Validation of tax returns and benefit entitlements.
- Analytics-enabled verification and progressive debt collection.

## Why a new employee should understand it

CVB owns publicly described collections and verification programs such as ARNI. Understanding CVB is essential when reading collections audits, inventory metrics, decision-support systems, and regional workload interactions.

## Related branches

### Officially supported relationships

- Program headquarters branch ([[CRA-Program-Branches]]).
- Org-chart label sometimes uses Collections and Verifications (plural); mandate heading uses Verification (singular).

### Derived onboarding interpretation

> These connections are vault onboarding aids. They are **not** official CRA reporting lines.

- Complements [[02-Organization/Branches/Compliance Programs Branch|CPB]] on integrity of the tax system (derived functional pairing; not an official org-chart line).
- Regional delivery and inventory effects are explicit themes in the ARNI audit involving CVB and regions.

## Related public audit and evaluation cases

# Compliance Programs Branch

## Full name and acronym

- **Full name:** Compliance Programs Branch
- **Acronym:** CPB (Status: current — supported by official public CRA sources and/or published CRA audit/evaluation reports)
- Preferred short link: [[Compliance Programs Branch|CPB]]

## Classification

Publicly classified as a **program branch** among CRA headquarters branches (Ministerial Transition 2025 Organization page: 6 program / 8 corporate headquarters branches, plus Corporate Secretariat and 4 regions).

## Public mandate

Protects the integrity and fairness of the Canadian tax system through education and proactive efforts aimed at helping those who want to comply, and making it harder for those who choose not to comply. Addresses and deters non-compliance through a graduated compliance approach including targeted education and communications, examinations, audits and, where warranted, penalties or criminal investigations. Administers various tax credit programs in a timely, consistent, and prudent manner.

## Main public responsibilities

- Education and proactive compliance support.
- Examinations, audits, penalties, and criminal investigations where warranted.
- Administration of various tax credit programs.

## Why a new employee should understand it

# Legislative Policy and Regulatory Affairs Branch

## Full name and acronym

- **Full name:** Legislative Policy and Regulatory Affairs Branch
- **Acronym:** LPRAB (Status: current — supported by official public CRA sources and/or published CRA audit/evaluation reports)
- Preferred short link: [[Legislative Policy and Regulatory Affairs Branch|LPRAB]]

## Classification

Publicly classified as a **program branch** among CRA headquarters branches (Ministerial Transition 2025 Organization page: 6 program / 8 corporate headquarters branches, plus Corporate Secretariat and 4 regions).

## Public mandate

Acts as the ultimate authority for the interpretation of tax and benefits related legislation. Establishes and clarifies the interpretation of tax laws and is responsible for recommending legislative amendments to the Department of Finance on behalf of the CRA. Holds responsibility for registering and regulating charities and the income tax treatment of registered plans, and for excise and specialty tax programs.

## Main public responsibilities

- Authoritative interpretation of tax and benefits legislation; GST/HST rulings and legislative policy.
- Charities registration/regulation and registered plans.
- Excise and specialty tax program administration (excise duty/tax, fuel charge, luxury tax, air travelers security charge).
- Recommending legislative amendments to the Department of Finance on behalf of the CRA.

## Why a new employee should understand it

LPRAB explains why charities, rulings, and legislative interpretation appear in audits separately from Compliance Programs. The Charities Audit Process case is an LPRAB MAP owner example.

## Related branches

### Officially supported relationships

- Program headquarters branch ([[CRA-Program-Branches]]).
- Official partnership context: CRA provides Finance Canada input on proposed legislative changes ([[CRA-Organizational-Overview]] strategic relationships summary).

### Derived onboarding interpretation

> These connections are vault onboarding aids. They are **not** official CRA reporting lines.

- Charities compliance work is distinct from general [[02-Organization/Branches/Compliance Programs Branch|CPB]] audit programs even though both support tax-system integrity (derived clarification).

## Related public audit and evaluation cases

- [[Internal Audit - Charities Audit Process]] — Charities Directorate within LPRAB; LPRAB agreed to MAP.

## Related knowledge domains

# Security Branch

## Full name and acronym

- **Full name:** Security Branch
- **Acronym:** Not established as a standard short form in the official public sources used for this vault. Do not invent one.

Leads cross-cutting CRA projects for an integrated enterprise approach; improves service design and delivery with client centricity and accessibility; manages CRA data and information assets and related governance/quality frameworks; conducts strategic planning, performance measurement, and reporting; and coordinates relationships with federal, provincial, territorial, and Indigenous partners.

# CRA Acronym Dictionary

## Navigation path

```text
Acronym in this table
→ Canonical note (wikilink)
→ Branch mandate / classification
→ [[Ownership and Assurance Roles]] / related concepts
→ [[Public-Audit-Case-Map]]
→ Official SRC note (e.g. [[99-Sources/source-notes/SRC-CRA-Org-2025]])
```

Prefer `02-Organization/Branches/` notes. Legacy `01-Organization/* (legacy redirect)` files do not carry branch acronym aliases.

## Acronym verification rule

Acronyms are added as aliases only when an official CRA public source (organization page, published audit/evaluation, departmental results material, or similarly authoritative canada.ca page) uses or clearly establishes them. Do not invent acronyms from name initials alone.

Only acronyms supported by official public CRA/Government of Canada sources or existing vault case notes grounded in those sources. Status markers:

- **Status: current** — used in current official public materials
- **Status: historical** — appears in older public materials; not treated as current structure

# CRA Branch Relationship Map

This map organizes **functions**, not unsupported reporting lines. For ownership vs assurance vocabulary see [[Ownership and Assurance Roles]]. Case matrix: [[Public-Audit-Case-Map]].

Every relationship is labelled:

- **Official public relationship** — stated or clearly demonstrated in official public sources
- **Derived onboarding relationship** — vault explanation aid
- **Historical relationship** — older public naming or period-specific context

## Tax and benefit processing

- [[Assessment, Benefit, and Service Branch|ABSB]] administers key tax processing services, contact centres, and benefits — **Official public relationship** (mandate).
- Regions operate Tax Centres and Contact Centres for delivery — **Official public relationship**.
- ABSB ↔ regions for processing/service channels — **Derived onboarding relationship**.

## Compliance

- [[Compliance Programs Branch|CPB]] delivers graduated compliance (education through investigations) — **Official public relationship**.
- CPB ↔ [[Business Intelligence]]/[[Information Technology Branch|ITB]]/[[Service, Innovation, and Integration Branch|SIIB]] for analytics-enabled compliance — **Derived onboarding relationship**, reinforced by BI audit stakeholder lists (**Official public relationship** for those named interviews).

## Collections and verification

- [[Collections and Verification Branch|CVB]] delivers validation, verification, and collections programs — **Official public relationship**.
- CVB ↔ regions for ARNI and inventory controls — **Official public relationship** ([[Internal Audit - Accounts Receivable National Inventory]]).
- CVB ↔ CPB as complementary integrity functions — **Derived onboarding relationship**.

## Appeals and recourse

- [[Appeals Branch]] delivers impartial recourse services — **Official public relationship**.
- Appeals ↔ compliance/collections decisions that generate disputes — **Derived onboarding relationship**.
- Appeals AC role includes tax-litigation risk management — **Official public relationship** (AC biography/mandate context on org page).

## Policy and legislative interpretation

- [[Legislative Policy and Regulatory Affairs Branch|LPRAB]] is ultimate authority for interpretation of tax/benefits legislation and recommends amendments to Finance — **Official public relationship**.
- Charities Directorate within LPRAB — **Official public relationship** ([[Internal Audit - Charities Audit Process]]).
- LPRAB ↔ Finance Canada on legislative change — **Official public relationship** (strategic relationships section).

## Service, data and integration

- [[Service, Innovation, and Integration Branch|SIIB]] leads service design, data/information assets, performance reporting, and partner coordination — **Official public relationship**.
- SIIB AC = Chief Data Officer and Chief Service Officer — **Official public relationship**.
- OLO in SIIB for Ombudsperson liaison — **Official public relationship**.
- SIIB BI responsibility since 2011 with ITB service delivery — **Official public relationship** (BI audit).

## Information technology

- [[Information Technology Branch|ITB]] develops/operates/evolves CRA IT and provides solutions to CBSA — **Official public relationship**.
- ITB ↔ SIIB for BI service delivery and BIDGSC co-chairing — **Official public relationship** (BI audit).
- ITB ↔ Security Branch for EFMS maintenance — **Official public relationship** (EFMS audit).

## Digital transformation

- [[Digital Transformation Program Branch|DTPB]] sets enterprise digital transformation direction — **Official public relationship**.
- DTPB ↔ ITB/SIIB on digital change — **Derived onboarding relationship** (DTPB also interviewed in BI audit: **Official public relationship** as stakeholder).

## Internal audit, evaluation and enterprise risk

- [[Audit, Evaluation, and Risk Branch|AERB]] provides independent assurance, evaluation, and enterprise risk support — **Official public relationship**.
- AERB publishes via [[Internal Audit and Program Evaluation]] — **Official public relationship**.
- AERB as third line in cyber audit narrative — **Official public relationship**.
- AERB ↔ Audit Committee / Board oversight context — **Official public relationship** / governance pages.

## Finance and administration

- [[02-Organization/Branches/Finance and Administration Branch]] provides financial/resource management, administration, real property; AC is CFO — **Official public relationship**.
- Financial statements reviewed by Audit Committee and approved by Board — **Official public relationship**.

## Human resources

- [[Human Resources Branch|HRB]] provides HR advice/services/stewardship — **Official public relationship**.
- HRB ↔ workforce capability for program delivery — **Derived onboarding relationship**.

## Communications and privacy

- [[Public Affairs Branch]] provides communications, ATIP, and related public affairs services; AC is Chief Privacy Officer — **Official public relationship**.
- Public Affairs ↔ confidentiality/privacy regime — **Derived onboarding relationship** (org-page confidentiality section + ATIP reports).

## Security

- [[02-Organization/Branches/Security Branch]] protects people, information, and assets; centralizes security functions — **Official public relationship**.
- Security Branch formation / ASO role increase as of April 2022 — **Official public relationship** (cyber audit).
- Security ↔ ITB ↔ AERB Three Lines description — **Official public relationship** (cyber audit).

## Legal services

- [[Legal Services Branch]] / Department of Justice provides litigation and legal advisory services to CRA, Board, and Ombudsperson — **Official public relationship**.
- Legal Services ↔ Appeals litigation-risk themes — **Derived onboarding relationship**.

## Regional delivery

- [[Atlantic Region]], [[Quebec Region]], [[Ontario Region]], [[Western Region]] deliver programs via field offices — **Official public relationship**.
- Regions ↔ HQ program branches (technical/policy support) — **Official public relationship**.
- Regions ↔ corporate branches (enterprise services) — **Derived onboarding relationship**.

## Historical relationships

- [[Domestic Compliance Programs Branch]] — **Historical relationship**; do not equate to [[Compliance Programs Branch|CPB]] without an official succession source.
- Older transition pages listing **13** HQ branches — **Historical relationship**; current public baseline is **14** branches (2025).

## How to use this map with cases

```text
Public audit case
→ AERB (publisher / assurance)
→ named program/corporate branch (OPI / MAP)
→ ITB / SIIB / Security / regions when listed
→ related process, system, data, risk, control notes
```

See [[Organizational-Onboarding-Path]].

# CRA Governance Structure

## Stable role information (official)

Primary baseline: Ministerial Transition 2025 Organization page (chart, chart description, and Agency Governance Overview).

The CRA governance structure includes:

- a [[Minister of National Revenue]]
- a [[Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer]] (Deputy Minister equivalent)
- a [[Deputy Commissioner]] (Associate Deputy Minister equivalent)
- a [[Board of Management]]
- a [[Taxpayers Ombudsperson]] (arm’s length; accountable directly to the Minister; no authority in administration/enforcement of legislation for which CRA remains accountable to the Minister)

Supporting governance component:

- [[Corporate Secretariat]] — assists Board, Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, and senior management; supports corporate policy instruments; centre of expertise for GIC appointments

Official legend titles:

- [[Assistant Commissioner|AC]]
- [[Deputy Assistant Commissioner|DAC]]
- [[Regional Assistant Commissioner|RAC]]
- **ADM** — Assistant Deputy Minister
- **ED/SGC** — Executive Director/Senior General Counsel

## Board of Management (stable)

- Oversees organization and administration of the CRA and management of resources, services, property, personnel, and contracts
- Develops/approves Corporate Business Plan; approves Departmental Results Report and annual audited financial statements
- May advise the Minister on general administration/enforcement of program legislation
- May **not** direct the Commissioner or an employee in statutory powers or administration/enforcement of program legislation
- Not authorized to receive personal/business information obtained under program legislation

See [[Board of Management]] · [[Audit Committee]].

## Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner (stable)

**Commissioner and CEO**

- Day-to-day management and direction of the CRA
- Accountable to the Minister, the Board, and the Clerk of the Privy Council
- Ex-officio Board member

**Deputy Commissioner**

- Supports the Commissioner; exercises assigned duties; acts for the Commissioner in absence, incapacity, or vacancy
- Not a Board member but normally attends Board meetings

## Taxpayers’ Ombudsperson (stable)

- Arm’s length from CRA operations
- Accountable directly to the Minister
- Service-complaint, systemic reporting, and outreach mandate
- Official organizational relationship: Ombudsperson Liaison Office located in [[Service, Innovation, and Integration Branch|SIIB]]; SIIB AC (as Chief Service Officer) holds monthly bilateral meetings with the Ombudsperson

# Ownership and Assurance Roles

Derived onboarding note: it **composes** how different accountability roles fit together in CRA public-audit practice. It does **not** add official CRA org-chart reporting lines or titles beyond what public sources and case notes already state.

## What the CRA Organization page does and does not define

**Official public CRA facts** on [[CRA-Organizational-Overview]] and branch mandate notes include program vs corporate branches, [[Information Technology Branch|ITB]]’s IT mandate, [[Service, Innovation, and Integration Branch|SIIB]]’s data and service roles (including [[Chief Data Officer]] placement where sourced), and [[Audit, Evaluation, and Risk Branch|AERB]]’s independent assurance mandate ([[99-Sources/source-notes/SRC-CRA-Org-2025]]).

The public Organization page **does not** formally define every ownership term used in this vault—business-process owner, program owner, system owner, data owner, control owner, or audit client. Those labels come from **general professional concepts** (linked below), **case-specific** OPI/MAP language in published reports, and this **derived** relationship model.

## Relationship model

```text
Business / program branch (or named program area)
→ owns business outcome / process accountability
→ often appears as OPI and/or MAP owner in public audits

ITB or technical function
→ supports technology (build, run, evolve systems and services)
→ may be named co-responsible for technical MAP actions
→ does NOT automatically own the business process

Data owner / data-accountable role (e.g., CDO mandate; stewards per Data Governance)
→ governs data responsibility (definitions, quality, permitted use)
→ distinct from IT operations and from AERB assurance

Control owner (first line; sometimes split with technical custodians)
→ designs, operates, monitors, and remediates a specific control

Change requester → Change approver → Deployment authority
→ (derived teaching chain) initiate / authorize intent / authorize go-live
→ see [[Change Requester]], [[Change Approval]], [[Deployment Approval]]
→ technical implementers are not automatically approvers

AERB (third line / IA & PE)
→ independently audits or evaluates
→ may judge whether MAPs are reasonable
→ does NOT own the business process, system, data, or corrective execution
```

Management (not AERB) owns [[Management Response]] and [[Management Action Plan]] corrective action after [[Recommendation]]s. Ambiguous ownership is a control risk—see [[Unclear Accountability]].

## Content-class labels

| Class | Meaning in this note |
|---|---|
| **Official public CRA facts** | Branch mandates, ITB/SIIB/AERB roles as on Canada.ca org baseline |
| **Official case-specific facts** | Named OPI, MAP owner, or co-responsible parties in a published audit report |
| **Derived onboarding interpretation** | The composed diagram above; teaching use of “audit client” |
| **General professional concepts** | Linked concept notes (`content_origin: general-professional-knowledge`) |

## Worked example — Business Intelligence audit

Primary illustration: [[Internal Audit - Oversight Use and Continuous Improvement of Business Intelligence]].

| Role in the model | Who in this case (vault-supported) | Class |
|---|---|---|
| Business / program ownership of BI activities | [[Service, Innovation, and Integration Branch]] (SIIB) — BI responsibility since 2011; MAP lead | Official case-specific |
| Program users (not MAP lead) | Selected [[02-Organization/Branches/Compliance Programs Branch|CPB]] (CPB) and [[02-Organization/Branches/Collections and Verification Branch|CVB]] (CVB) teams (examined/interviewed) | Official case-specific |
| Technical support | [[02-Organization/Branches/Information Technology Branch|ITB]] (ITB) — BI service delivery; BIDGSC co-chair; collaboration in action plans | Official case-specific |
| Data leadership signal | [[Chief Data Officer]] = SIIB Assistant Commissioner | Official org + case-specific |
| Independent assurance | [[Audit, Evaluation, and Risk Branch]] (AERB) — publishing branch; judged MAPs reasonable | Official case-specific |
| Corrective action | SIIB agrees to strengthen BI governance (ITB/stakeholders named in plans) | Official case-specific |

This case shows why “BI involves technology” must not collapse into “ITB owns BI.”

Secondary illustration (split maintenance vs MAP lead): [[Internal Audit - Enterprise Fraud Management System]] — [[02-Organization/Branches/Security Branch]] MAP owner; [[Information Technology Branch|ITB]] co-named for selected actions; AERB publishes assurance.

### Worked example — ARNI (program branch OPI/MAP)

| Role in the model | Who in this case (vault-supported) | Class |
|---|---|---|
| Program / business ownership | [[Collections and Verification Branch|CVB]] — OPI / MAP owner for ARNI | Official case-specific |
| Technical / decision-support context | DSS and related systems discussed under CVB program context; enterprise BI use constrained (report themes) | Official case-specific themes |
| Regional delivery | Four regions in scope for workload controls | Official case-specific |
| Independent assurance | [[Audit, Evaluation, and Risk Branch|AERB]] — publishing branch | Official case-specific |

### Reporting accountability chain (derived teaching)

```text
Report / process owner (business outcome)
→ Data owner (definitions & quality)
→ Technical support (pipeline/platform)
→ Report-logic / change approver
→ Management Review (challenge before reliance)
→ AERB (independent assurance — not report owner)
```

See [[Management Reporting]], [[Management Review]], [[How Data Quality Affects Management Reporting]].

## Concept notes (ownership taxonomy)

### Risk and control roles

- [[Business Process Owner]]
- [[Program Owner]]
- [[System Owner]]
- [[Technical Support]]
- [[Data Owner]]
- [[Control Ownership]]
- [[Change Requester]]
- [[Change Approval]] (change approver)
- [[Deployment Approval]] (deployment authority)
- [[Unclear Accountability]]

### Audit and assurance roles

- [[Audit Client]]
- [[Internal Audit Independence]]
- [[Management Action Plan Owner]]

### Frameworks and related concepts

- [[Three Lines Model]]
- [[Change Management]]
- [[Management Action Plan]]
- [[Management Response]]
- [[Data Governance]]
- [[Scope]]
- [[Change Management Map]]
- [[Software and Data Onboarding Path]]

# Atlantic Region

## Geographic scope

New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Public program-delivery role

One of four CRA regions responsible for **program delivery via field offices** in their area of operation. Each region is led by a [[Regional Assistant Commissioner]].

Official public source describes regional operations in:

- **Tax Services Offices (TSOs)** — more complex audit, collection and related files with more direct taxpayer/representative interaction
- **Tax Centres (TCs)** — tax return processing centres
- **National Verification and Collections Centres (NVCCs)** — non-complex, non-face-to-face collections, validation, and verification
- **Contact Centres (CC)** — individual or business enquiries for tax and benefits
- **Northern Service Centres (NSC)** — three NSCs support individuals, community organizations and businesses in Yukon, Northwest Territories and Nunavut
- **Centres of Expertise (COEs)** — leadership, best practices, research, support and training for a focus area

Do not infer staffing structures beyond this public listing.

## Relationship with headquarters branches

### Officially supported relationships

- Regions deliver operational programs while six headquarters **program** branches centrally organize technical and policy support ([[CRA-Program-Branches]]).
- Eight headquarters **corporate** branches provide corporate services agency-wide ([[CRA-Corporate-Branches]]).

### Derived onboarding interpretation

> Not an official reporting-line diagram.

- Headquarters program branches set national program frameworks; regions execute workload through TSOs, TCs, NVCCs, and contact centres.
- Corporate branches (for example [[Information Technology Branch|ITB]] and [[02-Organization/Branches/Security Branch]]) support enterprise capabilities used in regional delivery.


## Relevant public audits or evaluations

- [[Internal Audit - Accounts Receivable National Inventory]] — examined CVB and regional controls across four regions.
- [[Internal Audit - Oversight Use and Continuous Improvement of Business Intelligence]] — interviewed BI Quality Assurance stakeholders in Western, Ontario, Quebec, and Atlantic regions.
- [[Internal Audit - Charities Audit Process]] — methodology included headquarters and regional offices.

## Office holders

> The 2025 ministerial transition organizational chart is a **historical public snapshot** for named individuals.

### Current office holder

**Not confirmed on a newer official CRA page as of last verified date.** Chart/region-section names are recorded under historical office holders only.

### Historical office holders (public snapshot)

- **Tanya Cameron** — Acting Regional Assistant Commissioner (a/RAC). Named on 2025 chart; branch/region text noted acting until June 2025 on that page.

## Source dates

- **Structure source date:** Organization page details **2025-09-09**

# Ontario Region

## Geographic scope

The province of Ontario and Nunavut.

## Public program-delivery role

One of four CRA regions responsible for **program delivery via field offices** in their area of operation. Each region is led by a [[Regional Assistant Commissioner]].

Official public source describes regional operations in:

- **Tax Services Offices (TSOs)** — more complex audit, collection and related files with more direct taxpayer/representative interaction
- **Tax Centres (TCs)** — tax return processing centres
- **National Verification and Collections Centres (NVCCs)** — non-complex, non-face-to-face collections, validation, and verification
- **Contact Centres (CC)** — individual or business enquiries for tax and benefits
- **Northern Service Centres (NSC)** — three NSCs support individuals, community organizations and businesses in Yukon, Northwest Territories and Nunavut
- **Centres of Expertise (COEs)** — leadership, best practices, research, support and training for a focus area

Do not infer staffing structures beyond this public listing.

## Relationship with headquarters branches

### Officially supported relationships

- Regions deliver operational programs while six headquarters **program** branches centrally organize technical and policy support ([[CRA-Program-Branches]]).
- Eight headquarters **corporate** branches provide corporate services agency-wide ([[CRA-Corporate-Branches]]).

### Derived onboarding interpretation

> Not an official reporting-line diagram.

- Headquarters program branches set national program frameworks; regions execute workload through TSOs, TCs, NVCCs, and contact centres.
- Corporate branches (for example [[Information Technology Branch|ITB]] and [[02-Organization/Branches/Security Branch]]) support enterprise capabilities used in regional delivery.


## Relevant public audits or evaluations

# Assistant Commissioner

## Role (not a person)

An **Assistant Commissioner (AC)** is a senior CRA executive who leads a headquarters program or corporate branch (or holds an equivalent senior title publicly listed for a branch).

## Public responsibilities

- Lead a headquarters branch listed on the CRA organization overview.
- Some ACs hold additional public titles (examples from the official org page): Chief Audit Executive; Chief Financial Officer; Chief Information Officer; Chief Data Officer and Chief Service Officer; Chief Privacy Officer; Digital Transformation Officer; Chief Human Resources Officer; Agency Security Officer.

## Legend (official)

Ministerial Transition 2025 Organization page legend: **AC: Assistant Commissioner**.

## Current office holders

Office holders change. See individual branch notes and the official organization page for named ACs. Do not treat any single AC name as permanent without checking a current official source.

## Why a new employee should understand it

Public audits and departmental plans often name an AC-led branch as program owner, MAP respondent, or stakeholder. Knowing the AC role helps you separate **branch accountability** from **individual incumbents**.


## Office holders

### Current office holder

Role title is stable. Individual incumbents are branch- or region-specific and must be confirmed on a current official page. Names on the 2025 organizational chart are **historical snapshot** only — see branch and region notes.

### Historical office holders

See the 2025 Organization page chart and the relevant [[CRA-Organizational-Overview]] conflict table. Do not promote chart names to “current” without a newer official confirmation.

# Corporate Secretariat

## Classification

**Other organizational component** — not one of the 14 headquarters branches. Official source states the CRA comprises 14 headquarters branches, a **Corporate Secretariat**, and 4 regions.

## Public mandate

Reporting to the Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner’s offices, the Corporate Secretariat assists the Board of Management, the Commissioner, the Deputy Commissioner, and senior management in decision-making by providing governance, logistic, and planning services to Chairs, members, and committees. It also supports management and oversight of CRA corporate policy instruments (CPIs) and is the Agency’s centre of expertise for Governor in Council appointments.

## Board Secretariat relationship

Officially supported: Board operations are supported by the Board Secretariat, led by a Director who reports to the Corporate Secretary, who reports directly to the Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner.

## Why a new employee should understand it

Corporate Secretariat explains how Board/committee logistics and corporate policy instruments are supported without confusing the Secretariat with AERB (assurance) or Public Affairs (communications/ATIP).

# CRA Departmental Results Framework

The CRA publishes a **Departmental Plan** and **Departmental Results Report** that together describe expected and achieved results, resources, and priorities in line with federal reporting practice.

## Elements captured in this vault (from provided sources)

### Direction

- [[CRA Vision Mission and Values]]
- [[CRA Mandate]]
- [[CRA Core Responsibilities]] — **Tax** and **Benefits**
- [[CRA Strategic Priorities]] — three priorities for **2026–27** (A, B, C)

### Resources and results

- **Planned** spending and FTEs for **2026–27** in [[CRA Performance Measurement]] and [[CRA Core Responsibilities]]
- **Actual** tax and benefits spending for **2024–25** in the departmental results report (see [[CRA Performance Measurement]])

### Departmental Results Framework (DRF)

The Departmental Plan **2026–27** presents results using the **Departmental Results Framework**. For the planning period, the framework includes **12 departmental result indicators**: **10** under the **Tax** core responsibility and **2** under **Benefits**. Indicator definitions, targets, and planned results appear in the plan tables; **actual** results for the prior year appear in the **2024–25** departmental results report.

Always label **planned** vs **actual** and the **fiscal year** when citing an indicator value.

### Governance linkage

[[Board of Management]] supports world-class administration and **develops the Corporate Business Plan**; the Commissioner manages day-to-day delivery ([[Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer]]).

### Assurance

[[Internal Audit and Program Evaluation]] provides independent assurance aligned with **International Standards for the Professional Practice of Internal Auditing**; audits are risk-based (IA landing page).

## Document pairing used here

| Document | Role | Period emphasized in vault |
|----------|------|----------------------------|
| Departmental Plan 2026–27 | Plans, priorities, planned resources | **2026–27 planned** |
| Departmental Results Report 2024–25 | Actual results | **2024–25 actual** |

02-Strategy-Performance/CRA Mandate.md.body:
# CRA Mandate

The CRA’s published **mission** states what the agency is charged to do on behalf of governments in Canada.

## Mission (Departmental Plan 2026–27)

The CRA will **administer tax, benefits, and related programs**, and **ensure compliance** on behalf of governments across Canada, thereby **contributing to the ongoing economic and social well-being of Canadians**.

## Relationship to responsibilities and governance

- Two **core responsibilities** are identified publicly: **Tax** and **Benefits** ([[CRA Core Responsibilities]]).
- Administration and enforcement are carried out under the [[Minister of National Revenue]] with day-to-day responsibility on the [[Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer]]; the [[Board of Management]] oversees organization and administration but not tax law enforcement.

## Context

See also [[CRA Vision Mission and Values]] and [[CRA Strategic Priorities]] for **2026–27** planning priorities.

## Sources

- [Departmental Plan 2026–27](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/corporate/about-canada-revenue-agency-cra/departmental-plan/2026-27-cra-departmental-plan.html)

03-Statistics/Assessment Cut-Off Date.md.title: Assessment Cut-Off Date
03-Statistics/Assessment Cut-Off Date.md.body:
# Assessment Cut-Off Date

**Individual Income Tax Return Statistics** include assessments and reassessments processed only up to a stated **cut-off date**. Returns assessed or reassessed **after** that date are excluded until a later edition or [[Statistical Revision]].

## 2025 edition — 2023 tax year

For the edition covering the **2023 tax year**:

- Statistics contain the most recent 2023 tax year **assessments or reassessments** up to **November 30, 2024**.
- The **2025 edition** presents data based on 2023 tax year returns **filed and processed** up to **November 30, 2024**.

## Timeliness change

Starting with this edition, CRA uses an **earlier extraction cut-off** (**November 30, 2024**) instead of **June 30, 2025** (prior approach referenced on the official page) to **increase timeliness**. When comparing this edition to earlier ones, **differences in extraction time frames** must be considered ([[Comparability Across Editions]]).

## Relationship to filing statistics

Operational filing volumes (for example [[Electronic Filing Statistics]] for fiscal year **2024–25**) use different reporting periods and definitions than this assessment cut-off.

## Sources

- [Individual Income Tax Return Statistics (2023 tax year) — Explanatory notes](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/programs/about-canada-revenue-agency-cra/income-statistics-gst-hst-statistics/t1-final-statistics/2023-tax-year.html)
- [[Individual Income Tax Return Statistics]]
